notes: Local names in Ibaloi, Kankanaey or Ifugao depending on the naming community; binomials are codex-only and never appear in observation prompts.
Entries flagged needsReview are not confirmed by a local speaker yet: confirm before ship or gate them behind the guide quest.

species.description: Tall montane pine of the Cordillera ridges, with a broad open crown and a straight resinous trunk. Fire-adapted and fast on disturbed slopes; old trees carry thick, fire-scarred bark.
observationTraits: Needles 15-20 cm long, bundled three to a sheath
Cones short, ovoid, sitting sideways on the branch
Bark deeply fissured, dark at the base and redder higher up
species.season: Cones ripen Oct-Feb; fresh needles flush with the monsoon

codex.summary: The saleng is the landmark tree of Baguio ridges: wood, resin and shade for a whole old-growth canopy.
codex.campusContext: Stands on the ridge above the campus slopes.
codex.ecology: Fast canopy coloniser; casts a deep floor mat of needles, holds soil on steep drops, and seeds after fire.
codex.cultural: Resin-saturated 'saleng' splinters burn slowly and were carried as torches; timber for ridge houses, coffins and ritual posts.
codex.status: Blue-listed as a threatened Philippine pine on heavily cleared parts of its range; planted widely on campus.

species.description: Mountain-endemic lily with huge white trumpet flowers held upright on a single stalk above a skirt of narrow grassy leaves. Flowers after the first heavy rains.
observationTraits: Trumpet flowers white with a faint red-purple wash, facing up the stalk
Narrow grassy leaves set all around the lower stem

codex.summary: A Philippine-endemic lily of highland slopes; when in flower its white trumpets are visible from the path.
codex.campusContext: Kept to sunny pathside shoulders on the lower terrace.
codex.ecology: Bulbous geophyte, flowering after the first heavy rains; depends on moth and hawk-moth pollinators.
codex.cultural: Grown and traded as a cut flower in Baguio and La Trinidad; bulbs collected from the wild.
codex.status: Least concern globally, but local populations thin where roads and building cut the bulbs.

species.description: Tree-fern with a single fibrous trunk and a crown of two-metre fronds unfurling from coiled croziers. Its presence marks cool, permanently damp old-growth edges.
observationTraits: Trunk single and fibrous, no branches
New fronds unroll from tight croziers at the crown
Fronds spread in one plane; no flowers, no cones, no seed
species.season: Fertile all year; new croziers in the wet season

codex.summary: Tree-ferns are rainforest plants of damp shade; a grove of them means the slope has stayed wet for years.
codex.campusContext: Sheltering the damp retaining wall of the upper sanctuary edge.
codex.ecology: Reproduces by spores, not seed; the crown channels fog and rain down the fibrous trunk into the root mat.
codex.cultural: Bracken of other species is gathered for vegetable and medicine; tree-fern trunks are sometimes split for orchid mounts.
codex.status: Varies with taxon; collection of wild trunks for gardens is the common pressure.

species.description: Woody epiphyte that perches on pine trunks: leathery leaves in stiff whorls, pink to purple bracts and berry clusters hanging under the leaf crown, not at the tip.
observationTraits: Leaves in whorls around the stem, not paired alternately
Flower and berry clusters hang beneath the leaf crown
Older stems woody, rooted to another tree's bark
species.season: Flowers most of the year; berries after flowering

codex.summary: An epiphyte that grows on living pines, not on the ground; the whorled leaves and hanging berry clusters give it away.
codex.campusContext: One whorl sits on a saleng trunk where it forks.
codex.ecology: Epiphyte, not parasite; birds eat the berries and carry the seed between pines.
codex.cultural: Sold in Baguio and La Trinidad markets as an orchid-like ornamental; some Medinilla are taken from pine bark for sale.
codex.status: Several Philippine Medinilla are endemic and range-restricted; many are collected from the wild.
threats: Removal from host trees for sale
codex.localNameConfidence: name to confirm with a Kankanaey speaker

species.description: Highland pitcher plant of mossy seeps and creek banks: a long tendril hangs down into a fleshy cup with a hard ribbed peristome (rim) and a lid over its mouth.
observationTraits: Cup hangs at the end of a long tendril, mouth pointing up
Rim of the mouth raised into hard ribs
Lid open above the mouth; cup underside dark red
species.season: Pitchers all year, longest in the rainy season

codex.summary: A carnivorous highland speciality of mossy seeps; the cup catches insects in fluid and looks nothing like a flower.
codex.campusContext: Two plants in the mossy pocket of the sanctuary edge, past the guide's introduction.
codex.ecology: Pitcher fluid and slick lips trap insects; the habitat is cool, splashed and permanently wet.
codex.cultural: Gathered over it as a curiosity; several highland species are sold from the wild.
codex.status: Many Philippine highland Nepenthes are narrow endemic to one or two mountains.
